newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: ABORIGINES TO SEND ABUSE LIST TO EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT
A European Parliamentarian says he is very interested in seeing a dossier of alleged human rights abuses against Aborigines.
The Northern Land Council says it will send the parliament the dossier, which focuses on proposed changes to native title laws.
Hugh Kerr, who's on the parliament's delegation to Australia and New Zealand, says the documents would be discussed with the Australian delegation of the European Parliament.
He says the Human Rights Sub-Committee of the parliament would also be interested because of their recent statement on the importance of the human rights clause in the Australian trade agreement.
EUROPEANS WILL DISMISS HUMAN RIGHTS DOSSIER
Acting Foreign minister Ian McLachlan says he doesn't think the European Parliament will take much notice of a Northern Land Council dossier of alleged human rights abuses against Aborigines.
Australia's refusing to sign a trade agreement with the European Union while it contains a human rights clause.
The Australian government says trade and human rights should not be linked.
The Northern Land Council says the dossier will focus on proposed Government changes to native title laws.
Australia is proposing a separate document covering human rights.
TOURIST COMMISSION WINS INTERNET AWARD

The Australian Tourist Commission's Internet site has won an international award. It's been named the best "Destination" site in the prestigious Enter 97 Web Awards in Scotland, beating Microsoft's Expedia travel site and the Internet Travel Network. Commission managing director, John Morse, says the award is recognition of the way technology is transforming the tourism industry.
CALLS FOR INQUIRY OVER DEATHS IN NSW INSTITUTIONS
The New South Wales Council for Intellectual Disabilities is calling for a judicial inquiry into suspicious deaths of disabled people in public and private institutions.
The council's chairman, John Jacobsen, was commenting on a homicide investigation today into seven deaths at the Woodstock Centre for the Disabled in Albury between 1992 and 1994.
He says the number of deaths could rise to seventy before anything is done.
AUSTRALIA'S HIGHEST MOUNTAIN MAY CAUSE MAP MAYHEM
The spelling of Mount Kosciusko's name could be in for a change.
The New South Wales government is trying to make a decison on whether to change the name to match the spelling of Polish hero Tadeusz Kosiuszko, after whom the mountain is named.

His surname has a z as the third last letter not the current s. The NSW government has invited submissions which close today. The current spelling of Kosiusko has appeared on every map published since 1840.
Land Minster Kim Yeadon says a body known as the Geographic Names Board has the task of solving the name dilemma.
QLD UNION LEADER SAYS BLAME SANTORO FOR INDUSTRIAL STRIFE
A Queensland union leader says state Industrial Relations Minister Santo Santoro should be blamed for the rise in industrial action new industry laws will cause.

Last night Queensland's state Parliament passed laws that will outlaw compulsory unionism, reform unfair dismissal procedures and change the nature of the award system and industrial agreements and ACTU General Secretary John Thompson has described the new laws as the worst in Australia and says they will cause disputes in workplaces that have never seen industrial action before.
He says workers under the state award system will move to the federal system as a result of the laws.
MAKING NEWS IN SPORT
Cricket...West Indies manager Clive Lloyd has criticised his selectors for not choosing an all rounder or a spinner on the tour of Australia.
Lloyd was speaking on the eve of the fifth test at the WACA.
SHEFFIED SHIELD
At the MCG, Victoria resumes today at 1 for 12 in reply to the New South Wales total of 290.
While Western Australia is 4 for 102 in response to Queensland's first innings total of 179.
RUGBY LEAGUE
Penrith ultility back Ryan Girdler is flying to Townsville this morning after his late call up to the Australian side for the World Nines which starts this afternoon.
Girdler replaces Laurie Daley who has a back injury.
Australia plays the United States in their opening game.
GOLF
The second round of the Vines Golf Classic is underway in Perth. Greg Turner leads on 7 under, one clear of Frank Nobilo.
Wayne Grady is a further stroke back.
SWIMMING
Olympic swimming champion Alexander Popov looks set to return to competition at the Canberra Sprint meet on February 22. Popov hasn't raced since he was stabbed on a Moscow street after the Olympics.
